statement: After eliminating one pivot from an n-live-variable canonical CNF, every non-tautological raw clause is a distinct signed clause over the r=n-1 remaining variables. There are exactly 3^r such clauses including the empty clause. If any independent argument gives at most K distinct raw clauses, define K*=min(K,3^r). Then total raw literal mass is at most Wmax_r(K*), and engine raw_units<=1+K*+Wmax_r(K*). If c retained clauses and at most R distinct resolvents are possible, one may take K=c+R. The same bound gives post-canonical m'<=K* and L'<=Wmax_r(K*).
proof: For each of the r remaining variables, a non-tautological clause has exactly three choices: absent, positive, or negative. Hence the complete signed-clause universe, including the empty clause, has 3^r elements.

The engine raw container is a set. Retained clauses are inserted into this set and each non-tautological resolvent is inserted only if it is not already present. Therefore retained clauses and resolvents share one global distinct-clause universe; their width budgets cannot be maximized independently using the same widest clauses twice.
Among K* distinct signed clauses over r variables, maximum total width is Wmax_r(K*), obtained by selecting clauses in descending width. Width-w multiplicity is C(r,w)2^w.
The engine resource measure is state_units(raw)=1+|raw|+sum_{C in raw}|C|. Thus raw_units<=1+K*+Wmax_r(K*).
Canonicalization, subsumption and later unit propagation cannot increase clause count or literal mass, so m'<=K* and L'<=Wmax_r(K*) are safe downstream bounds.
